title: Destrier box manifest
description: Describes how Destrier builds, runs, and evaluates a box. Every box contains a single `box.yaml`.

id.description: A unique, immutable identifier. Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only.

version.description: Semantic version (for example, 1.0.0). Increment it whenever the box changes. Never modify a published version.

name.description: A human-readable name for the box.

authors.description: One or more author names or handles.

runType.description: The type of environment the box runs in: a single container, a single virtual machine, or a multi-host network.

category.description: The skill areas covered by the box, for example web, privilege-escalation, lateral-movement, or binary-exploitation.

difficulty.description: The validated difficulty of the box.

objective.description: A one-line description of what the agent must achieve to solve the box.

flags.description: The flags available in the box. Each flag represents a capture point, such as a user or root flag on a host, or one flag per host in a multi-host box.

host.description: The host that contains this flag. Must match one of the hosts defined below.

gating.description: The privilege required to retrieve this flag. The flag is generated for every run and is never committed to the box.

network.description: The network the agent's harness connects to at the start of the evaluation. Must match one of the defined networks.

networks.description: The networks that make up the box. Most boxes use a single network, while network boxes typically define several.

name.description: The network name, referenced by hosts and the entrypoint.

hosts.description: The hosts that make up the box. Container and virtual machine boxes usually contain one host, while network boxes contain multiple.

name.description: A unique name for this host.

build.description: The path to the host's build definition. This is typically a Dockerfile directory for containers or a Packer definition for virtual machines.

os.description: The guest operating system. Defaults to Linux if omitted.

networks.description: The networks this host is connected to. A host connected to multiple networks can act as a pivot point.

healthcheck.description: Optional. How Destrier verifies the host is ready before the evaluation begins. Omit this field if the host has no service to check. Supported formats: tcp:PORT, http:PORT/path, and https:PORT/path.

wallClockSeconds.description: The maximum wall-clock time allowed for a single evaluation.

maxCostUsd.description: The maximum model cost allowed for a single evaluation, enforced by the platform.
